theorem: Let phi: R -> S be a ring homomorphism. Then ker(phi) is an ideal of R.
assumptions: phi: R -> S is a ring homomorphism

nodes.claim: Let a and b be in ker(phi). Then phi(a) = 0 and phi(b) = 0.
nodes.self_contained_claim: Let a and b be in ker(phi). Then phi(a) = 0 and phi(b) = 0.

nodes.claim: We have phi(a - b) = phi(a) - phi(b) = 0, so a - b is in ker(phi).
nodes.self_contained_claim: We have phi(a - b) = phi(a) - phi(b) = 0, so a - b is in ker(phi).

nodes.claim: Thus ker(phi) is closed under subtraction.
nodes.self_contained_claim: Thus ker(phi) is closed under subtraction.

nodes.claim: Therefore ker(phi) is an ideal of R.
nodes.self_contained_claim: Therefore ker(phi) is an ideal of R.
